question: What device did John Ambrose Fleming invented in 1904 that helped make radio, television, telephone and even early electronic computers possible?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Oscillation valve.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **John Ambrose Fleming** invented the oscillation valve, also known as the **Fleming valve**, in **1904.**
 
• The oscillation valve was **a two-electrode vacuum tube** that could** rectify alternating current (AC) into direct current (DC).**
 
• This invention was crucial for the development of** radio, television, telephone, and early electronic computers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Voltaic pile** was invented by **Alessandro Volta in 1800.** It was an early form of electric battery.
 
• The** point-contact transistor** was invented by **John Bardeen**, **Walter Brattain, and William Shockley in 1947**. It was the first fully operational semiconductor device.
 
• The** electrodynamometer** was invented by **Andre-Marie Ampere in 1820**. It was an early instrument used to measure **electric current**.
